gen-dafont-college-gf-hind-madurai: College hits with a dynamic, authoritative punch, every curve as heavy as its straight stems and the counters big. Hind Madurai follows in a plain sans, approachable and neutral, its lowercase filling the line so paragraphs move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-college-gf-hind-mysuru: Loud, heavy display letters up top, then a contemporary sans below with lowercase tops pressed close to the ascender height. And because Hind Mysuru drops the calligraphic thinning, the lighter text never fights the weight of College.
gen-dafont-college-gf-hind-siliguri: Authoritative, with big counters and curves as thick as its stems, College takes the lead. Hind Siliguri settles beneath it as sans-serif text, a flat gray hum of constant line weight that feels approachable across a long stretch.
gen-dafont-college-gf-hind-vadodara: College's curves are as thick as its straight stems, which gives its tall lowercase a bold, dynamic feel. Hind Vadodara is the quieter partner, with spacious gaps in its rounds.
gen-dafont-college-gf-huninn: Huninn reads modern and tidy, its lowercase rising close to cap height. Beside College, with curves as thick as its stems, it takes a modest text size while the heading carries the authority.
gen-dafont-college-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight reads crisp and modern, like bent tubing, with short ascenders and curve tails held back. And College gives it a dynamic, authoritative heading whose thick curves and big counters carry the page's weight.
gen-dafont-college-gf-karla: Karla reads modern and approachable, its gaping c opening and tall middle band making each line look stocky. Over many paragraphs it feels sturdy and friendly.
gen-dafont-college-gf-kedebideri: Kedebideri, a sans-serif with a skyward x-height and rounded, inviting letters, handles the text. But College earns its keep big and brief, where stems and crossbars share one thickness and the tall lowercase can show off.
gen-dafont-college-gf-khula: College is dynamic and authoritative, drawn so every curve matches its straight stems, with big counters in a tall lowercase. Khula does the quieter job as a plain sans, its tall midsection and open curves carrying running text.
gen-dafont-college-gf-krub: Krub reads contemporary and neutral, with a pronounced x-height and curves that lift off before closing the loop. College supplies the dynamic push, while Krub's sans-serif text keeps a steady hand beneath it.
